body.statement: Every member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\) has full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\), is causally sufficient, and is pairwise identifiable in the sense of Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin; hence it belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\).
body.justification: The proposition proves that the nonlinear certificate family lies inside the direct-law identifiable CPCM class.
body.gap: Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin defines pairwise identifiability and recovers a CPCM DAG from its direct law but does not verify those conditions for this paper's stricter Poisson-root positive-polynomial benchmark family.
body.consumer: It validates the causal model class searched by the reusable certificate.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\) and one type \(r\).  In a topological ordering, every root Poisson mass is strictly positive, and every non-root conditional Poisson mass is strictly positive because its rate is an intercept plus nonnegative terms with a strictly positive intercept.  Therefore
\[
\Pr_\theta(V=v)=\prod_{s=1}^p
p_{rs,\theta}(v_s\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{d_r}(s)})>0
\quad\text{for every }v\in\mathbb N_0^p. \tag{12}
\]
This proves full support.

Let \(U_{rs}\), over all nodes and types, be mutually independent
\(\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) variables.  Generate each root and then each non-root in topological order by the generalized inverse of its stipulated Poisson conditional distribution evaluated at \(U_{rs}\).  This realizes exactly (12), and the exogenous variables are jointly independent.  Hence causal sufficiency holds.

It remains to verify the stated pairwise condition.  Fix an edge \(k\to s\) and any admissible conditioning set \(S\) with
\[
\operatorname{pa}(s)\setminus\{k\}\subseteq S
\subseteq\operatorname{nd}(s)\setminus\{k,s\}.
\]
By (12), the event \(V_S=0\) has positive probability, and conditional on this event the retained cause \(V_k\) has support \(\mathbb N_0\).  With all other parents fixed at zero, the effect rate is
\[
\lambda_s(x)=\alpha_s+b_{sk}x^{q_{sk}},
\qquad \alpha_s>0,\quad b_{sk}>0,\quad q_{sk}\in\mathbb N. \tag{13}
\]
The DAG factorization gives the local Markov property, so conditioning additionally on nondescendants in \(S\) that are not parents does not change this conditional kernel once all parents are fixed.
It is strictly increasing and unbounded.  The cited Poisson-CPCM reversibility result says that a nonidentifiable bivariate Poisson direction must instead have rate \(\exp(ax+b)\) with \(a<0\), which is strictly decreasing.  Thus (13) cannot be exceptional.  Every required conditioned pair is identifiable; when there are no edges the requirement is vacuous.  The three defining conditions of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\) now hold, proving inclusion.
